caveats: Identity boundary: Jong Pong Ju is the officially alleged worker identity charged in N.D. Ga. No. 1:25-CR-291; Bryan Cho is an officially alleged employment alias. Chollima Group separately maps Bryan Cho to Jong Pong Ju and assesses a likely Bureau 61/Umnal affiliation, but legacy Chris Yu, atroboj, atroobj, and bugarnet identifiers remain a reported cluster and are not merged into the legal identity without stronger selector-level evidence.
Charges are allegations; the subject is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

evidence.locator: Kim Kwang Jin et al. Indictment – Northern District of Georgia section, first paragraph
evidence.quote: Today, the Northern District of Georgia unsealed a five-count wire fraud and money laundering indictment charging four North Korean nationals, Kim Kwang Jin (김관진), Kang Tae Bok (강태복), Jong Pong Ju (정봉주) and Chang Nam Il (창남일)

A five-count indictment unsealed Monday in the Northern District of Georgia names Kim Kwang Jin, Kang Tae Bok, Jong Pong Ju, and Chang Nam Il as defendants in the case, accusing them of wire fraud and money laundering.
Since at least in or about May 2021 and continuing until in or about February 2022, defendant JONG PONG JU, using the alias ‘Bryan Cho,’ was employed by Company-2 to provide IT services.

On or about February 11, 2022, defendant JONG PONG JU, using access granted to him by Company-2, fraudulently obtained virtual currency tokens valued at approximately 60 Ether (worth approximately $175,680 at the time of the theft) from Company-2

sourced_facts.label: Media-reported collective reward of up to $5M (State Department Rewards for Justice, as reported)

evidence.quote: The FBI has offered a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to the arrest of the four men.
JONG PONG JU a/k/a ‘Bryan Cho,’ and CHANG NAM IL a/k/a ‘Bong Chee Shen,’ a/k/a ‘Peter Xiao,’ were citizens of North Korea
In truth, ‘Peter Xiao’ was actually defendant CHANG NAM IL, which defendant JONG PONG JU knew at the time he recommended ‘Peter Xiao’ to Company-2.

sourced_facts.label: Allegedly sent stolen funds to mixer

evidence.quote: On or about February 13, 2022, defendant JONG PONG JU sent virtual currency totaling approximately 60 Ether that was fraudulently obtained from Company-2 to Tornado Cash for mixing.

The defendants, KIM KWANG JIN, KANG TAE BOK, JONG PONG JU, and CHANG NAM IL, and others unknown to the Grand Jury, traveled to locations outside of North Korea, including the United Arab Emirates, using North Korean travel documents, and lived and worked as a co-located team.
The defendants are believed to have traveled to the United Arab Emirates in 2019 on North Korean travel documents and worked there together as a co-located team.
